newsitem.title: BRAZIL: No talks planned between Brazil stevedores, Cosipa.
newsitem.headline: No talks planned between Brazil stevedores, Cosipa.

text.p: No new talks were scheduled Monday morning to resolve an impasse between striking stevedores at Brazil's Santos port and Companhia Siderurgica Paulista (Cosipa), a spokeswoman said.
"The impasse continues. There are no talks scheduled at the present time," said a spokeswoman for the steel firm.
Twenty-six stevedores have been occupying two vessels at Cosipa's private terminal at Santos port for almost two weeks.
They are protesting the firm's decision to use its own workers to load and unload at the terminal.
The strike is for the time being only affecting the Cosipa terminal.

As of Monday morning, 17 vessels were docked at the port including four at private terminals. All but the two ships docked at the Cosipa terminal were operating normally, said a port authority spokesman.

The stevedores have warned they will immediately call a general strike if military police stationed on the pier try to evict union members on the boat or if Cosipa allows new vessels to dock at the terminal and uses its own workers.
Unions at the port were holding a meeting Monday morning at the stevedores' headquarters. ((-Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151))
